summary: DAY expectations/execution review covered every company in the Chief-selected 12-name active batch while keeping Earth quality separate from opportunity/timing. No normalized live price/consensus/crowding feed is treated as a T0 baseline requirement; where unavailable, those fields remain unknown rather than blocking company promotion. Execution asymmetry is widest in NBIS, OKLO, BTDR and IONQ because capital intensity, commercialization/acquisition effects and financing can dominate outcomes; SYM, MRVL, COHR, LITE, MPWR, CLS and APH carry shared AI-capex expectation risk; PL retains government-budget/event sensitivity. All 12 are advisory ready_for_chief from this lane, independent of underwriting blockers.

perCompanyCoverage.executionView: Large committed demand increases forward visibility but also raises pre-delivery capex/financing and customer-concentration sensitivity. Without normalized live valuation, no price-timing conclusion is asserted; realized cluster economics and funding structure are the key execution bridge.
unknowns: Committed capex/debt bridge, cluster margins and third-party mix

materialFindings.finding: All 12 companies are advisory ready_for_chief from expectations/execution because normalized live price, consensus and crowding are not locked T0 baseline inputs; their absence remains explicit unknown rather than a baseline blocker.

NBIS, OKLO, BTDR and IONQ have the widest execution dispersion because financing, commercialization/acquisition normalization and milestone delivery can dominate outcomes even if structural relevance is strong.

MRVL, COHR, LITE, MPWR, CLS and APH share an AI-infrastructure expectation factor; strong operating results can still produce poor execution outcomes if capex expectations reset or concentration is underappreciated.

BTDR's Q2 cash-flow structure is a direct execution warning: substantial operating/investing cash use was offset by heavy financing inflows. This does not falsify the thesis but demands financing-aware opportunity treatment later.

contradictions: Strong business execution can raise the expectation hurdle and therefore reduce investment attractiveness without lowering Earth quality.
Large contracts/cash balances can reduce demand/runway uncertainty while increasing concentration, dilution or financing sensitivity.
Acquisition-driven growth can improve strategic breadth while making short-horizon comparability and valuation more difficult.
unknowns: Normalized current price, market capitalization, sell-side consensus, options/crowding and short-interest inputs are not canonical T0 inputs in this pass and remain unknown where not independently normalized.
No price target, entry zone or Action State is asserted for these companies from non-canonical market data.

peerRequests.request: Do not block baseline promotion solely for missing non-canonical live market/consensus/crowding precision; keep those values unknown until a reproducible execution feed exists.
Keep NBIS/OKLO/BTDR/IONQ/SYM company-quality gates independent of this lane's advisory readiness and explicitly normalize financing/acquisition/concentration inputs before promotion.
Carry shared AI-capex factor concentration forward into later portfolio/execution calibration without contaminating long-horizon Earth Score.

accuracyDebates.reason: Prevents unavailable or noisy market-timing data from blocking T0 baseline quality while preserving it for later capital decisions.
Cash runway and funding structure can dominate realized shareholder outcomes even when technology/demand theses remain intact.
